---
title: "Figure 3.2: Commodity Prices"
---

![Python: `python/fig-3-2.py`](../images/python/fig-3-2.png)

Daily prices of six commodities that matter for the region's exports,
indexed to 1 January 2025 = 100. A value of 120 means the price is 20
percent higher than at the start of 2025. Oil is drawn thicker, to stand
out, and a dotted line marks the start of the Middle East conflict. Gold rose much more than the others and is drawn on a
right-hand scale, so that the other five keep enough room to be read.

This is the most involved of the line charts: it brings together date
filtering, a right-hand scale, an event marker and a legend for both scales.
Each of these is explained on an earlier page; the new part is the control
of which scale is drawn on top.

**New in this chart:**

- a different line width per series;
- drawing the left-scale series *on top of* the right-scale one;
- a legend that covers both scales.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 4369 rows of daily data from 2010. The columns are Oil,
Copper, Iron ore, Soybeans, Coffee and `Gold (right scale)`. The chart uses
January 2025 to September 2026:

```python
START, END = pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01"), pd.Timestamp("2026-09-30")
data = data[(data["category"] >= START) & (data["category"] <= END)]
```

## The script

### Series with their own widths

```python
# Series: (colour, line width). Oil is drawn thicker.
left_series = {
    "Oil": ("#0065A0", 2.2),
    "Copper": ("#00A6B2", 1.2),
    ...
}
gold = "Gold (right scale)"
gold_style = ("#FFA500", 1.2)
```

Each dictionary value is now a pair (colour, width), because the published
chart emphasises oil with a thicker line. The loop unpacks the pair:

```python
for series, (colour, width) in left_series.items():
    ax.plot(data["category"], data[series], color=colour, linewidth=width,
            solid_joinstyle="round")
```

### Gold on the right-hand scale, underneath

```python
# Gold is on the right-hand scale; draw it first so the others lie on top.
ax_right = add_right_axis(ax, (100, 220), 30)
ax_right.plot(data["category"], data[gold], color=gold_style[0],
              linewidth=gold_style[1])
ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)
ax.set_zorder(ax_right.get_zorder() + 1)
ax.patch.set_visible(False)
```

A twin axes object normally lies on top of the original one, so gold would
cover the other lines. In the published chart, it lies underneath. Two lines
fix this:

- **`set_zorder`** puts the left-scale axes object on top.
- **`ax.patch.set_visible(False)`** makes its background transparent, so the
  gold line underneath is not hidden by it.

See [A right-hand scale](../techniques.qmd#sec-right-scale).

### The conflict marker and the axes

```python
ax.axvline(CONFLICT, color="black", linewidth=1.0, linestyle=(0, (1, 1.5)))
ax.text(CONFLICT - pd.Timedelta(days=8), 73, "Middle East conflict",
        fontsize=9.7, fontstyle="italic", ha="right", va="bottom")

ax.set_xlim(START, END)
ax.set_xticks(pd.date_range(START, "2026-09-01", freq="4MS"))
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b-%y"))
ax.spines["bottom"].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=90, length=0, pad=5)

set_y_scale(ax, 70, 190, 30)
ax.axhline(100, color="black", linewidth=0.7)
```

- **The x-axis** has a label every four months. Its axis line is drawn at
  100 (the index base) instead of at the bottom, as in [Figure
  3.1](fig-3-1.qmd).
- **The line at 100** was missing in the R version generated by the
  pipeline. It is part of the published chart.
- **The two scales** both span 120 with a tick every 30: 70–190 on the left
  and 100–220 on the right. Their ticks are therefore at the same heights,
  as in the published chart.

### One legend for both scales

```python
legend_styles = {**left_series, gold: gold_style}
ax.legend(
    [Line2D([], [], color=c, linewidth=w) for c, w in legend_styles.values()],
    list(legend_styles),
    loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 1.0), fontsize=8.6,
    handlelength=2.6, labelspacing=0.05,
)
```

The legend shows all six series with their own line widths.

- `{**left_series, gold: gold_style}` makes one dictionary of all six
  series, with gold last, as in the published chart.
- The list comprehension unpacks each (colour, width) pair into `c` and `w`
  and makes a sample line (`Line2D`) with that style, so oil is thick in the
  legend too.
- `fontsize=8.6` and `labelspacing=0.05` make the legend compact, so six
  entries fit in the top left without touching the lines.

Because `ax` is now the top layer, the legend goes on `ax`. In most other
two-scale charts it goes on `ax_right`; the rule is the same in both cases:
put the legend on whichever axes object is on top.

## Changing the chart

- **A new period.** Change `START`, `END` and the last tick date. The daily
  data go back to 2010, so the filter can select any period. For a longer
  period, label every six or twelve months (`freq="6MS"` or `"12MS"`).
- **A different base date.** The data are indexed to 1 January 2025. To
  rebase to another date, divide each column by its value on that date:

  ```python
  base = data[data["category"] == pd.Timestamp("2026-03-02")].iloc[0]  # a date in the data
  for col in [*left_series, gold]:
      data[col] = data[col] / base[col] * 100
  ```

  and update the subtitle and the line at 100.
- **Gold on top.** Delete the `set_zorder` and `patch.set_visible` lines.
  The twin axes object is then on top again, and the legend should move to
  `ax_right`.
- **Emphasise another commodity.** Change its width in `left_series`, for
  example `"Copper": ("#00A6B2", 2.2)`. The legend follows.

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-3-2.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-3-2.py"}
"""Figure 3.2: Commodity Prices."""
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

from chart_style import (
    add_right_axis,
    new_chart,
    read_chart_data,
    save_chart,
    set_y_scale,
)

STEM = "fig-3-2"

START, END = pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01"), pd.Timestamp("2026-09-30")
CONFLICT = pd.Timestamp("2026-03-01")

data = read_chart_data(STEM)
data = data[(data["category"] >= START) & (data["category"] <= END)]

# Series: (colour, line width). Oil is drawn thicker.
left_series = {
    "Oil": ("#0065A0", 2.2),
    "Copper": ("#00A6B2", 1.2),
    "Iron ore": ("#C55A11", 1.2),
    "Soybeans": ("#7F7F7F", 1.2),
    "Coffee": ("#5DADE2", 1.2),
}
gold = "Gold (right scale)"
gold_style = ("#FFA500", 1.2)

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="Commodity Prices",
    subtitle="(Index: January 1, 2025 = 100)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: Bloomberg Finance L.P.; and IMF staff calculations.\n"
        "Note: Oil is the average petroleum spot price. Copper is from the London\n"
        "Metal Exchange. Iron ore is Shanghai SteelHome E-Commerce.\n"
        "Soybeans is from the Chicago Board of Trade. Coffee refers to the\n"
        "international coffee composite indicator price."
    ),
    title_size=13.5,
    caption_size=8.25,
    left=0.4,
    right=0.4,
    bottom_gap=0.55,
)

# Gold is on the right-hand scale; draw it first so the others lie on top.
ax_right = add_right_axis(ax, (100, 220), 30)
ax_right.plot(data["category"], data[gold], color=gold_style[0],
              linewidth=gold_style[1])
ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)
ax.set_zorder(ax_right.get_zorder() + 1)
ax.patch.set_visible(False)

for series, (colour, width) in left_series.items():
    ax.plot(data["category"], data[series], color=colour, linewidth=width,
            solid_joinstyle="round")

ax.axvline(CONFLICT, color="black", linewidth=1.0, linestyle=(0, (1, 1.5)))
ax.text(CONFLICT - pd.Timedelta(days=8), 73, "Middle East conflict",
        fontsize=9.7, fontstyle="italic", ha="right", va="bottom")

ax.set_xlim(START, END)
ax.set_xticks(pd.date_range(START, "2026-09-01", freq="4MS"))
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b-%y"))
ax.spines["bottom"].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=90, length=0, pad=5)

set_y_scale(ax, 70, 190, 30)
ax.axhline(100, color="black", linewidth=0.7)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)

legend_styles = {**left_series, gold: gold_style}
ax.legend(
    [Line2D([], [], color=c, linewidth=w) for c, w in legend_styles.values()],
    list(legend_styles),
    loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 1.0), fontsize=8.6,
    handlelength=2.6, labelspacing=0.05,
)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
